function: Over-the-air FL (AirComp) with uplink TopRand sparsification and downlink grouped quantization; excluded for system: single-antenna clients and server, scalar per-subcarrier channel, no RIS (p. 4).
notes: Excluded for system (check 6), shown on p. 4. Checks 1 to 5 pass: it is a research article that proposes and evaluates TopRand global sparsification with automatic budget allocation for the uplink and grouped mixed-precision quantization with index sharing for the downlink; as federated learning over the air it passes no_learning; the design is the AirComp transmission of model updates, not an above-PHY function such as scheduling (clients are selected at random, p. 13, Algorithm 2); and the uplink aggregation is analog AirComp over OFDM subcarriers (p. 4, eqs. 6-11), so its function is area 7. But every client-server link has a single antenna at both ends and there is no RIS: p. 4: "h_{t,n}(i) ∼ CN(0, 1) is the coefficient associated with the i-th subcarrier between the n-th client and the server", with per-subcarrier truncated channel inversion (eq. 7) and the superimposed received signal y_t = Σ λ_t h_{t,n} ∘ (β_{t,n} ∘ s_{t,n}) + w_t (eq. 9); p. 9: "the wireless channels from the clients to the central server follow an IID Rayleigh distribution with zero mean and unit variance". The paper never mentions antennas, MIMO, beamforming, or a RIS (the only "MIMO" is in an author biography, p. 20), so the single-antenna setting follows from the scalar per-subcarrier channel model rather than from an explicit statement. If the reviewer judges it eligible, its area is 7. The PDF is the paper of the DOI (title and DOI 10.1109/JIOT.2025.3591626 on p. 1).
